item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I don't know what kind of ethics committee runs Marshall, Carter & Dark, but the casual sacrificing of six Level One security personnel kinda grates on me. I get that it's for a covert deal between them and the Foundation, but did they really need to waste their manpower like that? That kind of treatment is similar to how the Foundation treats their D-class, and even then they are careful not to waste valuable resources.

Plus the fact that a loving father would agree to the killing of six innocent men doesn't seem right to me. It's one thing to kill for an assassination, but letting your own men die is a whole other level. Kinda steered me away from liking Aleksander much.

A neutral for me. Still, it was good writing.

item.content:encoded:
Oh my.

I've been lurking for quite some time, but MC&D entering the Resurrection scene is definitely my wheelhouse.

At first I thought Aleksander was simply being ordered to go undercover, but the truth is far more interesting. Like Cyclopian, I love the concept of the Foundation trading resources with a distinctly hostile GOI under the table.

Also like Cyclopian, my only nitpick is Moss Heart's lack of characterization besides "I'm damn good at killing and I love my daughter," but I have faith that that will be fixed… Hell, this is as far as I've read in the series, so maybe it's ALREADY fixed.

Thanks for the tale!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
There's too much goofy shit, like having the main character named Aleksander Foxx, for me to take this seriously. It's too boring for me to appreciate it as goofy fun. The characters are too flat for me to appreciate it as a character piece. The writing is the weakest that I've seen in the series so far1 with bizarre flourishes like "sea-black coffee," "and an elderly man waltzed in," and "smiled a wicked grin" pulling me out of the story at pretty much every other line.

There were some moderately interesting aspects to the story, and there's some stuff that you mentioned earlier that I would like to see explored. But as a piece standing on its own merits, I have to give this a -1.

Footnotes
1. Which isn't to say it's bad. It's middling. But middling next to "some of the best writers on the site" represents a weird drop in quality.

item.content:encoded:
Like I had said in chat, I like the first half (since that portion was the entire article back then). I wish to talk about the second half, after the item swap.

  • I was initially iffy with the SCP documentation. It was referred to as "he" in-article for that portion. Of course, it ended off just when it is about to describe the anomaly. Now I wonder what does "Moss Heart? mean?
  • The idea of Huntsmen is intriguing. Not sure if other SCPs/Tales did it, but it could be an angle to look at for MC&D concepts.
  • Now if I'm not mistaken, Foxx's current allegiance is to the Foundation. Or will he toe the line between the 2 organisations?

I was initially sceptical of this work, but the idea of a (possibly) anomalous person leading a relatively normal life (with a family to boot) is something we don't get all that often here. You could explore on Foxx's relationship with his daughter (I would imagine it to be scenarios where the triad father refuses to let their kid know of their business).

item.content:encoded:
This is a part of Resurrection. It was not properly entered as such because… likely, because we confused L0rdDeath, so he didn't know the process for adding it.

However, this was edited with the assistance of the other Resurrection writers and approved for inclusion on the hub (anyone can write a story for Resurrection, it's only hub inclusion that needs approval).

Even though it is in the negatives, it is fully part of the canon until & unless it gets deleted. As such, I'm going to go ahead and add it to hub now.

(EDITx3: Wow, go moose. He actually did add it to the hub, just did it in a funky way.)

As I mentioned on IRC, this does border on cheese for me, and parts are imperfect, but I enjoy the characterization and world-building enough that it works for me. I really like the Huntsmen conceptually, and Foxx walks the 'cheese line' just enough that he works for me. The emphasis of his home life helps with this in particular.

Nitpick
– hide block

A small side note: Skitter Marshall doesn't match Resurrection's 'compatibility requirement' for matching accepted general mainline canon (such as it exists) for the Mister Marshall (see: Thank You For Your Time, Acquisitions Hub, and linked works on Acquisitions), but as I said on IRC, this could simply be another family member, with Jeremy Marshall being the Marshall, and Skitter has no reason to say otherwise. And I like that character quite a bit, actually.

I would suggest that Foxx have a thought that it might or might not be the Marshall, but that's up to L0rdDeath.

EDIT: Oh gods, I forgot about Wills And Ways Hub. Okay, yeah, then we definitely can go with multiple Marshalls with no concerns. And if the tale survives, let's probably link that tale for the reference :]

– hide block

I enjoy this, regardless of whether it bites the dust. +1'd. :)

EDIT x2: Also, note, though, just because something is part of Resurrection, doesn't mean it can't be extensively edited even if future articles have already been created building off of it. This is one reason we have a group — to take care of these sorts of snarls. Feedback away.
